title: Cofiltered split neighbourhoods compute the base stalk
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and let $y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ be a geometric point with $\Omega$ algebraically closed [def-weil-geometric-point]. A split neighbourhood consists of a pointed etale neighbourhood $(U,u)$ of $y$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] and pairwise disjoint clopen pieces of $U\times_Y X$, indexed by the geometric fibre, covering the base change, with the marked point $(u,t)$ in the $t$-th piece. Its morphisms are pointed neighbourhood morphisms mapping each piece into the corresponding piece. This category is cofiltered, and its forgetful functor to pointed etale neighbourhoods of $y$ is initial.

source.place: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.SplitNbhd.initial_forget; the existing fully proved split-neighbourhood argument underlying Stacks Tag 03QP (1)

proof.text: The existing theorem exists_hom constructs a split refinement of every pointed neighbourhood, using an affine chart and the finite-algebra splitting.
Pull back decompositions along common pointed refinements to construct cones for pairs of split neighbourhoods. Equalize parallel maps by a pointed refinement. This proves cofilteredness.

For each pointed neighbourhood, a split refinement exists; any two such choices admit a common split refinement, and parallel comparison maps can be equalized. Therefore the corresponding costructured-arrow category is connected, proving initial_forget.
